VPN service contract: a version, the engine's report of itself, and enums that grow, so an engine or an app of another make or release can keep to the contract (docs/client-architecture.md, "The version and the engine's report", "Keeping to the contract"; its C# types are its reference). The app writes the options in the highest version both sides speak (VpnServiceOptions.ContractVersion, VpnServiceContract.Negotiate) and VpnServiceHost refuses one it does not speak (Verify); with none in common the connect fails with VpnServiceContractException, naming both; options from before versions read as the first. An engine reports its versions and its optional features (VpnEngineInfo, with VpnEngineFeatures: a switch for each of split tunneling by app, the kill switch, the proxies, QUIC, the ads, always-on and the endpoint strategy, and the tracker kinds it makes): the head declares its engine's (AppOptions.VpnEngineInfo, VpnHood's own by default), and the engine writes the same in its status (ConnectionInfo.VpnEngineInfo). VpnHoodApp offers and asks nothing the engine lacks: AppFeatures, the ad providers, the kill switch's service, the app lists, the proxies, always-on and the trackers. An enum the contract carries reads a name it does not know as its JsonEnumFallback instead of failing the file (JsonStringEnumFallbackConverter, VpnHood.Net.Toolkit), each fallback the safe one to act on - ClientState Connecting, SplitUnsupportedIpMode Block, ProxyProtocol Socks5 - and the log level as Information; EndPointStrategy keeps writing numbers, for older clients reading tokens, and reads an unknown one as Auto. A tracker crosses as its kind and settings (TrackerFactoryInfo.Kind): ga4 with its measurement id, which any engine can speak, and dotnet for any other factory, made again from its type as before. In VpnHood.AppLib.App, CS8509 is an error and CS8524 silenced, as its DTO converters keep no default arm on purpose. Tests: VpnServiceContractTest walks every type the contract carries and checks each enum's fallback, the version and the report; VpnEngineTest, the app with a bare engine; TrackerFactorySerializerTest, the kinds.
chore(release): 1.0.13

Apple TV: the packages and the release build it. tvOS is a standard target of every Apple library and head (VhAppleTargetFrameworks: net11.0-ios and net11.0-tvos), so the packages carry it; the VhAppleTv property and the heads' guard are gone. CI's package and iOS jobs install the tvos workload. Publish-IosApp.ps1 publishes a head's tvOS target as <title>-tvos.ipa when the signing marker has the Apple TV's profiles, which Initialize-CiIosSigning.ps1 takes from TVOS_PROVISION_APP_BASE64 and TVOS_PROVISION_EXT_BASE64 (both or neither; without them the iOS build is as before), and the upload job sends it to the same App Store record as an Apple TV build. The Apple TV app has no update json of its own: it is the same head, and checks the iOS one. VpnHood.AppLib.Stores.AppStore takes VpnHood.AppLib.Stores.AppStore.Native 9.0.11, its first with tvOS, which every Apple build now needs. Docs: deployment.md's secrets, the forks' apple-app-store.md (the tvOS App Store profiles, the tvOS platform on the app's record), the iOS build doc and the heads' READMEs. Checked: the Apple libraries for iOS and tvOS on Windows, and CLIENT's iOS and tvOS and CONNECT's tvOS simulator builds on the Mac, against a local pack of 9.0.11.

Apple TV: the privacy texts cover it. The Apple TV build is the iPhone app's second target, with its AppDelegate and so its forced null tracker: it sends no usage data either. The CLIENT and CONNECT privacy policies say Apple devices - iPhone, iPad and Apple TV - wherever they said iOS (Effective 2026-11-03; the website takes them from develop), APP_STORE_PRIVACY.md says it holds for the Apple TV build under the same App Store record, and the first-run summaries say "Except on Apple devices" in all 13 languages (VpnHood.AppUi.Assets.Classic).
